About this job

In this internship, you will build tools that automate how Lightmatter creates and checks the mechanical drawings behind our advanced photonic packages. As a member of the Packaging team, you will build a toolset that generates substrate and package drawings and runs GD&T sanity checks on them. The capability you build will be used on all upcoming substrate and package tapeouts, so your work will go into real product development from day one. You will also work on experiments that feed into a fundamental understanding of coupled thermal-structural-optical physics.

You will be mentored by experienced packaging engineers while learning how package stack-ups, tolerancing, and drawing standards come together in leading-edge products for AI and high-performance compute. You will also see how drawing quality affects assembly, optical alignment, and reliability.

Responsibilities:

- Build tools to automate the creation of substrate and package drawings from package design data, reducing manual CAD and drafting effort.

- Develop automated GD&T sanity checks that catch common drawing errors before release, such as missing or inconsistent callouts, datum scheme issues, and tolerance conflicts.

- Work with packaging, substrate design, and system engineers to capture drawing requirements, templates, and conventions, and turn them into repeatable workflows.

- Validate your tools against existing released drawings and iterate based on feedback from engineers using them.

- Plan and execute physical DOEs, including test setup, measurement, and data analysis, to build fundamental understanding of coupled thermal-structural-optical physics.

Requirements:

- Currently pursuing a BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering or a related field.

- Coursework in Engineering Drawing, Manufacturing Processes, Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer, Engineering Mechanics, Strength of Materials, Design of Machine Elements, and Computational Design.

- Programming proficiency in Python (or a similar language) for scripting, data processing, and automation.

- Familiarity with CAD tools such as SolidWorks or Creo.

- Hands-on prototyping experience through coursework, capstone projects, research labs, or personal projects. Experience building, iterating, and validating physical assemblies is strongly valued.

- Willingness and curiosity to learn from an exciting team!

Preferred Qualifications

- Exposure to Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) and tolerance analysis concepts, including ASME Y14.5.

- Internships, capstone, thesis, or research projects involving precision mechanical assembly, optical systems, or microelectronics packaging.

- Experience using AI/ML tools or LLMs to build design automation workflows, such as automating tolerance analysis, CAD scripting, FMEA generation, or simulation post-processing.

Keysight's AI team builds adaptive engineering intelligence systems where measurement, simulation, and machine learning converge. This PhD internship focuses on the agentic layer that makes those systems usable for engineering teams.

You will design, build, and evaluate an agentic flow that takes a new use case from an engineering team and stands up a modeling and optimization workflow with minimal manual configuration. The agent analyzes available data, proposes and validates a setup, connects to approved tools needed to execute it, and explains both its choices and its results back to the engineer.

A central constraint is that the agent's output must be auditable and reproducible. Engineers need to see why a configuration was chosen, correct it, and re-run it deterministically. This includes building a benchmark of representative engineering use cases and establishing how reliably the flow completes bounded tasks with appropriate human oversight.

- Build an agentic flow that configures data preparation, model training, and optimization for a new use case with minimal input from the user.

- Build explainability into the flow, including why a configuration was chosen, what the resulting model depends on, and how confident it is.
- Design guardrails such as validation before expensive runs, bounded actions, and compute budgets so failures are cheap and visible.
- Assemble a benchmark of representative engineering use cases with objective success criteria, and measure task-completion reliability and result quality against an expert-configured baseline.
- Apply agentic AI to realistic engineering modeling and optimization workflows while developing practical experience evaluating non-deterministic systems.
- Collaborate across AI research, software engineering, RF design, and test and measurement domains.

- Experience with multi-agent systems or agent frameworks, and with MCP or comparable tool-integration protocols.

- Build an AI system that works across engineering tools and supports multi-step engineering tasks.

- We build the agent runtime itself — Codex / Claude-Code-class — not prompts on top of a vendor API.
- Evaluation and experimentation are first-class systems, not an afterthought. A self-improving loop optimizes whatever signal you give it, so the hardest and most valuable engineering here is making the judgment trustworthy — not just making the model change.

By combining generative recommendation, large recommendation models, multimodal representation learning, and cross-domain value modeling, the team works on some of the most important algorithmic problems in live commerce. - Context & memory for long multi-turn agents. Agentic memory (structured note-taking), context compaction / summarization, context editing / observation masking, and just-in-time (retrieve-then-load) retrieval. - The self-evolving loop. Case mining → automatic root-cause → constrained candidate generation → replay verification against frozen regression sets → canary → flywheel.
